anomalies.observed: The VREF-setting divider for the Nutrient-A TMC2209 (U6) uses R26 = 4k1 with R27 = 10k, while the pH and Nutrient-B drivers (U5, U7) use 4k7 with 10k. This gives U6 a VREF of about 3.55 V versus about 3.40 V for the other two drivers.
anomalies.expected: The three identical TMC2209 dosing-pump channels should use the same VREF divider values so that all three peristaltic pumps run at the same programmed current; the spec describes R24–R29 as the VREF-setting resistors for the three drivers without indicating any per-channel difference.

evidence.quote: R26 4k1 / R27 10k (Nutrient Pump A, U6 VREF divider)
R24 4k7 / R25 10k (pH Pump, U5) and R28 4k7 / R29 10k (Nutrient Pump B, U7)
5VOUT ... used locally to bias each driver's own current-reference divider (/5V_pH, /5V_NA, /5V_NB nets feeding VREF-setting resistors R24–R29)

anomalies.impact: Nutrient-A pump current would be set slightly higher than the pH-Down and Nutrient-B pumps, causing inconsistent dosing volumes between the three peristaltic pumps.

parsed.summary: The schematic is largely consistent with the specification, but the Nutrient-A TMC2209 VREF divider (R26 = 4k1) differs from the identical pH and Nutrient-B dividers (4k7), which would set a different motor current for that one dosing pump. No other clear deviation from the intended design was found.
